findings.title: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated for every request and crashes when member is None
findings.body: Line 71 unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member`, regardless of whether `optimized_pagination` was requested. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional (`RpcOrganizationMemberSummary | None`) and is None whenever the caller is not an organization member — e.g. org auth tokens, API keys, or a superuser acting on an org they don't belong to. Those requests now raise `AttributeError` and return a 500 for a previously working endpoint. Additionally, `has_global_access` is not a field on `RpcOrganizationMemberSummary` (global access is exposed on the request's `Access` object, i.e. `request.access.has_global_access`), so this attribute lookup will fail even when `member` is populated. Move the check behind the `use_optimized` flag and use a real, existing access API.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator's item key/cursor conversion is numeric-only and breaks the audit log's `-datetime` ordering
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, self.key)))` and `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` verbatim. The only caller (`organization_auditlogs.py`, `order_by="-datetime"`) sorts on a `DateTimeField`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`, producing a 500 as soon as the optimized path is taken. Even if that were fixed, `value_from_cursor` would hand an integer millisecond value to `build_queryset`, which injects it into `WHERE "datetime" <= %s` and compares a timestamp column against an integer, causing a database error. `DateTimePaginator` exists precisely to do these conversions; the new class cannot be used with a datetime sort key.

findings.title: Negative, user-controlled cursor offsets are passed straight into a Django queryset slice
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set, a cursor with `offset < 0` (cursors come from the untrusted `?cursor=` query parameter via `Cursor.from_string`, which accepts negative integers) is used as the slice start: `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset` negative. Django raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` on querysets, which is not caught by `Endpoint.paginate` (only `BadPaginationError` becomes a 400), so any request with a negative cursor offset returns an unhandled 500. The in-code justification ("the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", "permissions are checked at the queryset level") is incorrect, and it deliberately removes the negative-offset guard (`BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`) that every other paginator in this module enforces. Negative offsets should be rejected, not forwarded.

findings.title: Silent offset clamping in BasePaginator yields incorrect pagination instead of a clear error
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behaviour for every paginator derived from `BasePaginator`. For forward cursors a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0, but the raw negative `offset` is still used to build the next/prev cursors in `build_cursor` (e.g. `_build_next_values` computes `next_offset = offset + limit`), so a client passing a negative offset gets page-0 rows together with cursors that skip or repeat rows rather than a deterministic error. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed unclamped to the queryset slice, which raises `ValueError` from Django. Also note the subsequent check at line 192 (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still uses the unclamped `offset`, so it no longer matches the number of rows actually fetched.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported, contradicting the paginators
findings.body: The added comment states that negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization ... enables efficient reverse pagination", but no code changed here and every paginator in `sentry/api/paginator.py` (`OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, `CombinedQuerysetPaginator`, `CallbackPaginator`) explicitly rejects negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`. Leaving this comment in `Cursor.__init__` will mislead future readers into assuming negative offsets are a supported contract of the cursor type.

findings.title: Redirect-resolution loop bound silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop bound was changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000` and the explanatory comment ("theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. This is an unrelated, undocumented behaviour change: traces whose redirect chains are deeper than 1000 will stop resolving to their real root, so those segments get split into multiple partial segments and are emitted as if complete, with no error or metric to signal it. Either keep the previous bound or document/justify the reduction and add observability for hitting the cap.

findings.title: zunionstore uses the default SUM aggregate, corrupting end-timestamp scores on duplicate payloads
findings.body: `zunionstore set_key 2 set_key span_key` (and the same call for `parent_key` on line 53) uses Redis' default `AGGREGATE SUM`. Scores here are `end_timestamp_precise` values, and merges happen repeatedly as spans arrive. If the identical span payload is present in both merged keys — which happens with Kafka at-least-once redelivery or when a span is written under a parent key and later re-resolved — the resulting score becomes the sum of two epoch timestamps (~3.4e9), making that member permanently "newest". Since the new eviction logic (`zpopmin`) relies on these scores to drop the oldest spans, inflated scores cause the wrong spans to be evicted. Pass `AGGREGATE MAX` (or MIN) so the score keeps timestamp semantics.

findings.title: Span eviction limit is hardcoded to 1000 and drops spans with no metric or log
findings.body: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` silently discards spans. Two problems: (1) the limit is hardcoded in Lua while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is the configured knob — that parameter is now dead code and operators cannot tune the limit, and the two values disagree by one; (2) the previous behaviour logged an error and emitted `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` when a segment was too large, whereas the new path emits nothing, so oversized segments are now published as silently truncated segments that downstream consumers cannot distinguish from complete ones. Pass the limit in as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans` and emit a metric/return value when eviction occurs.

findings.title: `max_segment_spans` is now unused dead configuration
findings.body: The span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` was removed, so `self.max_segment_spans` (set from the constructor parameter on line 158) is no longer read anywhere; the span limit now lives as a hardcoded `1000` in `add-buffer.lua`. Anyone constructing `SpansBuffer(max_segment_spans=...)` will have their setting silently ignored. Either wire the value through to the Lua script's ARGV or remove the parameter.

findings.title: Unguarded `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` can crash the consumer on messages lacking the field
findings.body: `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` for any ingest-spans message that omits the field; the `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` on line 134 is a type-checker-only assertion and performs no validation, so a single malformed/older-format payload aborts batch processing and stalls the partition. Previously no span field beyond trace/span/project ids was mandatory. Consider defaulting (e.g. to the message/produce timestamp) or explicitly dropping such messages with a metric.

findings.title: No test covers the new insert-time eviction or score ordering
findings.body: The buffer tests were only mechanically updated to pass the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field. The core behaviour this PR introduces — zset-based storage, the 1000-span cap with `zpopmin` eviction of the oldest spans, and the removal of the old "skip too large segment" path — is completely untested. A regression in the Lua eviction arithmetic (e.g. popping too many spans, or evicting the root span) or in the zunionstore score aggregation would not be caught. Add a test that inserts more than the cap into one segment and asserts which spans survive, plus one asserting eviction keeps the highest `end_timestamp_precise` members.

findings.title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator has no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates ~70 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result` and adds a new `enable_advanced_features` code path, yet no tests were added in this PR for the class or for the modified offset handling in `BasePaginator.get_result`. Given the class is already broken for datetime keys and forwards negative offsets to the ORM, tests covering normal paging, prev cursors, and rejection of negative offsets are required before this can be relied on by an endpoint.
